baseline: Base commit plus the pending shared canonical streaming encoder; production source unchanged by these hash experiments.
workload: 30 fresh 1000-transaction collective fixtures per run; four serial validators; one-unit decrements; memory journals; test authentication; no real cryptography/network/fsync.
primary_comparison: Accelerated SHA-256 versus BLAKE3; both use identical SHA-256-asm mock signatures and verification. Software SHA-256 is a reference run whose mock authentication is also software SHA-256.
protocol_hash_scope: All production hashing sites in canonical.rs, typed_addr.rs and quorum/types.rs replaced in the temporary BLAKE3 variants; message/dialect/Merkle/quorum digests all use BLAKE3. Mock transaction signing remains a separate unchanged host layer.
wire_scope: Temporary algorithm substitution only. Existing equal-length wire labels/domain tags retained to isolate hashing cost; no BLAKE3-labelled wire protocol or compatible storage format was published or retained.
reproduce_build: Build each isolated checkout with CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_OPT_LEVEL=3 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP=true CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test --release -p cbcl-parser --test quorum_runtime --no-run. Enable sha2/asm for accelerated SHA-256 and both BLAKE3 variants. BLAKE3 uses default-features=false.
measurement: Three rotated rounds for initial variants; three alternating pairs for accelerated SHA-256 versus buffered BLAKE3; no concurrent builds/tests. Every workload asserted expected final counter value.
validation: Every benchmark run passed the expected final balance assertion. Buffered BLAKE3 checked against blake3::hash for nonuniform input lengths 0,1,63,64,65,511,512,1023,1024,1025,4096 and chunk sizes 1,7,64,1024.
decision: Retain SHA-256; accelerated SHA-256 won on this machine/workload. No BLAKE3 dependency or protocol change added to the working branch.
limits: Single Apple M2, short Merkle preimages and small transactions. Results do not establish the winner on x86, WASM or large payloads. Latest BLAKE3 tested using the installed toolchain; crate/MSRV integration was not attempted.
